$comment: Path floor for the UAT pipeline. Dimension one of two; see uat/capability-registry.json for dimension two. This file is the authoritative source: backend/src/modules/uat-pipeline/protected-paths.ts is a typed wrapper over it, and the CI diff gate reads these same bytes. A contract test asserts the wrapper deep-equals this file and that every non-glob path still exists on disk, so a silent rename cannot void a rule. Deny-tier itself: the pipeline can never edit this file.

tiers.deny: The pipeline halts before any LLM call. There is no override path in the product; only a human editing this file in a normal reviewed PR can change it.
tiers.review: The pipeline may proceed, but the checklist hard-blocks until a named human approver signs off, and the PR is labelled needs-domain-owner.

rules.reason: Payroll arithmetic is read-only by standing project rule. Quantify and report; never correct. The nightly recalc worker applies changes here retroactively.

Second, partially-duplicated payroll engine. It exports the same calculatePayrollRun/calculateGratuity/getPtFromSlab names as modules/payroll, so a change applied to only one is a silent correctness divergence.
Third salary engine, used at offer stage. Same divergence risk as payroll-compliance.
all-workers.ts is the single WORKERS[] registry for ~45 schedulers. A bad edit silences or double-runs every scheduled job, and a worker registered in only one place silently never runs.
Scheduled jobs run unattended; a fault here surfaces days later as missing data rather than as an error.
requireAuth, requireRole and scopeMiddleware are the enforcement points for every route in the application.
JWT signing, refresh-token rotation, 2FA and password reset.
Backend half of the dual-sided RBAC matrix. Drift between the two halves over-grants silently.
Frontend half of the dual-sided RBAC matrix. Must stay in sync with the backend copy.
Central authorization helper.
Row-scope enforcement. A change here can widen data visibility across branches and processes without any visible symptom.
Role resolution. Known to resolve demo-bypass identities to 'employee' via DB-driven lookups.
Demo bypass paths. Any change risks turning a demo affordance into a production authentication hole.
Runs DDL at process boot. A failed migration leaves health at 503.
Schema. Migrations apply automatically on restart; the pipeline is explicitly forbidden from introducing DDL (checklist DI-01).
Single validated env schema, including the kill switches and bypass flags (ENABLE_SCHEDULERS, INTERNAL_DEMO_BYPASS, PORTAL_DEMO_BYPASS, OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS, NCOSEC_RECONCILIATION_AUTO_FIX).
Payment gateway. Real money leaves the building through this code.
Salary disbursal and cheque validation.
Full and final settlement. Provisional-flag handling here gates whether an F&F can be approved at all.
P&L, budgets and billability. Finance period locks live here.
Vendor payments, GRN and cost centres.
Writes into attendance, which feeds payroll. Has an auto-fix mode gated only by an env flag.
Biometric ingestion. Attendance derived here becomes payable days.
The pipeline must never be able to modify the mechanism that decides whether its own modification is acceptable. Covers this file and capability-registry.json.
The pipeline's own implementation. Self-modification is prohibited by construction.
CI diff gate and related guards. A patch that edits its own gate could otherwise influence the gate evaluating it.
Mass-deletion guard and siblings.
Generates the migration manifest lock that the deletion guard checks against.
The test-count ratchet backing regression gates RG-01 and RG-02.
Migration governance and manifest guard tests.
The pipeline's own verification tests, including the workflow-verification suite.
Workflows, CODEOWNERS, issue templates and any secret-scanning configuration.

Secret-scanning configuration. Written as a glob deliberately: no gitleaks config exists yet, and a rule protecting a file that does not exist would fail the path-existence contract test while protecting nothing. As a glob it is exempt from that check and covers the file the moment someone adds it. .github/** already covers .github/secret_scanning.yml.
Route composition root. An additive app.use is the only change the pipeline could safely want here, and it is not worth the blast radius of allowing edits at all.
The deployed LMS is the external system of record. HRMS integrates, never rebuilds.
Client Portal. PII and payroll leakage risk to external client users.
Connection pools, circuit breaker and schema snapshot helpers.
Policy, route contract and data governance primitives.
Route composition. A new page must register here, so this is review rather than deny, but a mistake removes existing routes.
The pipeline must add tests, but must not weaken existing ones.
As above, for the backend integration suite.
Dependency and script changes. Checklist BR-07 blocks new dependencies outright; this catches script edits.
As above, for the backend.
